output.summary: An edible climbing gourd first cultivated in Mesoamerica between southern Mexico and Honduras. Its common fruit is wrinkled and roughly pear-shaped, with mild, watery flesh and one large flattened seed; the roots, stems, seeds and leaves are also edible.
output.edibilityNote: Fruit is eaten raw or cooked; roots, stems, seeds and leaves are also edible, with tubers cooked like root vegetables and shoots used in salads or stir-fries.
